deep.reconstruction:
This is folio 177r. Its main content is not mathematical. It is Riemann's pencil draft of the opening of his Latin petition to the Göttingen philosophical faculty for the doctorate (autumn 1851). The next page continues the petition and mentions the dissertation on the foundations of a general theory of functions of a complex variable, dated October 1851.

The Latin text reads: 'Ab amplissimo philosophorum ordine ea qua par est reverentia doctoris gradum petit G. F. B. Riemann, Breselenzius, stud. math. — Decane spectatissime, professores honorificentissimi! Mathematicae et physicae studio quum per quinquennium deditus fuerim, jam peto a vobis, viri maxime venerandi, ut ... meam [harum artium scientiam ...]'. In English: 'From the most distinguished order of philosophers, with due reverence, G. F. B. Riemann of Breselenz, student of mathematics, requests the doctoral degree. Most esteemed Dean, most honourable professors! Having devoted myself for five years to the study of mathematics and physics, I now ask you, most venerable men, that ... my [knowledge of these arts ...]'.

There are three groups of mathematical traces, written later or independently on the same sheet.

(a) Numbers in a lower-left block: 7,2379708 / 50 / 201, and 9,9680692 .. -0,929114 / 7,2379778. These are seven-place common-logarithm entries in the usual tabular convention, where the characteristic is offset by 10.
- My check: 9.9680692 - 10 = -0.0319308, and 10^(-0.0319308) = 0.929114. So '9,9680692 .. 0,929114' is a log-table lookup of the number 0.929114. The minus sign before 0,929114 in the manuscript presumably records the sign of the quantity, which logarithm tables do not encode.
- 7,2379708 corresponds to 10^(7.2379708 - 10), about 1.7297e-3.
- 7,2379778 differs from it by 70 units in the 7th decimal. This looks like an interpolation or correction step; the '50' and '201' may be table differences or proportional parts (my guess).
- What quantity is being computed cannot be determined from this page.

(b) '=6' at the lower right is an isolated scrap with no recoverable context.

(c) A formula is written vertically along the right margin. The image read with the next page's left-margin formulas shows it is the first of Riemann's series of formulas for Ω: Ω = -e(r,m)/(2m) * ( log(1-ξ) + φ0 + 2 Σ_{σ=1}^{m/4-1} log(1 - exp(2σ r/m · 2πi)) · exp(-σ^2 r/m · 2πi) ), for m ≡ 0 mod 4. These formulas belong to Riemann's fragment on the limiting values of elliptic modular functions, edited and commented on by Dedekind (Riemann, Werke, fragment XXVIII). There the logarithm of an eta-type theta series is evaluated as q tends to a root of unity e^{2πi r/m}. The evaluation is reduced to finite sums of log(1 - ζ^{2σ}) weighted by quadratic Gauss-type phases e^{-σ^2 r/m 2πi}, with a separate case for each residue class of m mod 4. On the next page this is derived via Ω' = Σ (-1)^n e^{-n^2 x i/m}/n, splitting n = σ + km and using Σ_k 1/(σ + km), evaluated by ∫_0^∞ x^{σ-1}/(1+x^m) dx.

On this page only the head of that formula appears; no derivation is carried out here.

The pairing of 7,2379708 and 7,2379778 (a difference of 7e-6 in the logarithm) cannot be assessed without knowing the intended quantity.

results.what: Seven-place log-table lookup: log10(0.929114) + 10 = 9.9680692, plus two nearby log values 7.2379708 and 7.2379778 with differences 50 and 201.
Heading of the Ω formula (m ≡ 0 mod 4) for the limiting behaviour of log of an eta/theta function at the root of unity e^{2πi r/m}, expressed through finite sums of logarithms with quadratic phases.
results.modern_name: transformation/asymptotics of log eta at cusps; precursor of Dedekind sums
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's fragment, published with Dedekind's commentary (1876/1892); Dedekind sums named after Dedekind

deep.surprise_reason: The page is the known draft of Riemann's 1851 doctoral petition. The only substantive mathematics is the margin heading of the Ω formulas from his modular-function fragment, which Dedekind already published with commentary. The numbers are routine log-table work.

checkable.asserts: approximately 9.9680690, matching the manuscript's 9,9680692 to table precision
the number whose tabular log is 7,2379708, about 0.0017297
the two log entries differ by 7.0e-6 (70 units of the 7th place)

transcription_corrections: The rotated right-margin formula is not 'D = εm/2m ...'. It reads approximately: Ω = -e(r,m)/(2m) (log(1-ξ) + φ0 + 2Σ ...) ... m ≡ 0 mod 4. It is the first of the Ω formulas continued in the next page's margin.
'Breselenzius' is written as a caret insertion after 'mann,', consistent with the {+...+} markup.
The struck word before 'meam' appears to be 'vob' (an abandoned 'vobis'), as transcribed.
'Riemann 18' at the top left and '(177)' are later archival annotations, not Riemann's hand.
